payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Make her close her jacket fully
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is the woman's jacket visibly closed more than in the input image, with its front panels brought together at least in part?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows the jacket's front panels brought together along some portion of the closure compared with the input. Fail if the jacket is visibly unchanged or more open. Unknown if the closure cannot be assessed from the image or comparison evidence is insufficient.
node.binding: Assess only the woman's jacket identified in the input image; judge visible change to its front closure, not unrelated edits.

node_traces.evidence: The jacket’s front is visibly more open in the edited image, with a panel hanging away from her body, rather than brought together compared with the source.

fulfillment: The node’s binding and completion criterion are already specific: the jacket must be fully closed, and the traces provide clear visual evidence that it remains open. The disagreement is not explained by an ambiguous criterion or a transport/schema failure; both checks executed successfully and consistently report failure. Do not weaken the closure requirement or reinterpret these failures as progress merely to match the reference. Instead, investigate whether the checks are comparing the correct source and edited images and whether the target jacket is reliably identified across the changed pose and viewpoint. The reference label constrains the aggregate but does not establish that the visible opening is absent; if the image evidence remains as reported, preserve the negative judgment rather than forcing agreement.
s2: The node’s endpoint criterion is clear, but its binding to “the same jacket and closure as in s1” may be brittle here: the edited image changes the woman’s pose and orientation, and the jacket front is partly obscured or motion-blurred. Avoid treating s1’s fail as proof of the final state; independently inspect the edited image and distinguish a genuinely visible closure gap from a loose, flared panel or an unobservable closure. Use unknown when the closure cannot be assessed reliably. The traces executed successfully, so this is not a transport/schema failure. The reference label alone does not establish full closure; do not force a pass or relax the requested endpoint without visual evidence.

response.content: {"text":"The binding is appropriately limited to the woman’s jacket, and the criterion already asks for a partial visible change relative to the source—not full closure. Do not tighten it to full closure or relax it to match the reference. The trace is valid and executed without dependency or transport failure, but its claim that the jacket is more open does not by itself resolve whether any requested progress occurred: the edited view changes her pose, and the front is flared and partly obscured. Improve the node’s comparison guidance so it assesses the same jacket and visible front-panel relationship across both images, distinguishing a genuinely unchanged/more-open closure from partial convergence and from an unassessable view. Preserve unknown when evidence is insufficient; treat the reference label as an aggregate constraint, not proof of a particular visual detail. Low confidence or repeated variation should prompt inspection, not be taken as evidence that the edit is absent."}
